findings.title: SQLite copies in the backup still open by path
findings.detail: Likely. _copy_file checks the SQLite magic through _open_exact, then sqlite3.connect(f'file:{src}?mode=ro') reopens by path and _refuse_moved(src) checks only afterwards. A hermes uid that swaps .hermes for a symlink and back during the online copy (inotify on its own home sees root's open; the swap-back keeps hermes_identity unchanged) can make root copy another root-readable SQLite DB, e.g. the gatekeeper DB, filed under a hermes: name with the hermes owner; a later restore of that archive installs it readable by hermes. Non-SQLite files have a smaller gap: _meta takes owner/mode from an lstat by path after the copy. Fix: verify that the main-DB fd sqlite opened (the new /proc/self/fd entry) has the dev/ino of the _open_exact fd (or compare dev/ino of the opened file before and after), take _meta from fstat of the verified fd, and optionally force hermes: entries to the hermes owner on restore; add a unit test for a swap during the copy.
